articles.title_orig: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
articles.title_zh: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
articles.content_orig:
Oracle is preparing to release security patches for 11 vulnerabilities in Java SE on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, all of which may be exploited remotely without authentication, as separate reports warn of a potentially critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw affecting OpenJDK.
The 11 vulnerabilities carry a maximum CVSS 3.1 severity score of 8.1, according to Oracle's advance security notice . The company has not disclosed their CVE identifiers, affected components, or the individual consequences of exploitation.
The separate OpenJDK vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 , has reportedly been assigned a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 and affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later. However, those details remain unconfirmed, and there is no evidence yet that the reported flaw is among the 11 vulnerabilities Oracle plans to patch.
Security firm Calif said in a post on X that it discovered and reported the flaw, which it calls Java4Shell , and that the vulnerability had leaked. Calif said it would publish technical details by 1 p.m. Pacific time on November 17, after Oracle releases a patch.
Security company watchTowr acknowledged the reports in a post on X , but cautioned that the technical details were still unconfirmed.
Separate analyses of the OpenJDK source code by security companies Upwind and Equixly point to a flaw in Java's Base64 decoder whose likely result is a crash of the Java virtual machine (JVM) rather than code execution.
The vulnerability's CVE record remains reserved without a public description. No official advisory has specified the vulnerable component, precise exploitation requirements, affected version range, or the availability of a fix.
Oracle's ops.java site now lists the replacement builds below as its current releases. Oracle's advance notice, release notes and download page still showed the earlier builds as of 16:59 UTC.
Oracle advises customers to stop using its current builds of Java 8, 11, 17, 21, 25, and 27 after the November 17 security update and move to the corresponding replacement releases.
The company's Java release notes contain the update guidance, while ops.java lists the following planned builds:
The November security notice identifies the following affected Oracle products and versions:
Oracle says all 11 Java SE vulnerabilities may be exploited over a network without requiring credentials. That does not necessarily mean they all allow remote code execution or that every application running an affected Java version can be attacked directly.
The advance notice does not identify the vulnerable Java components or specify what an attacker could accomplish by exploiting each flaw.
Oracle also warns that the information may change before the complete security advisory is published.
The reported CVE-2026-114938 vulnerability introduces a separate concern for organizations operating Java applications, particularly those exposed to the internet.
However, the public information does not establish whether the flaw affects the Java runtime itself, a particular library, or functionality that applications must expose for exploitation to succeed.
However, Oracle's notice and the OpenJDK advisories do not establish whether the flaw affects the Java runtime itself, a particular library, or functionality that applications must expose for exploitation to succeed.
Upwind said in a technical analysis that its reading of the OpenJDK source points to a flaw in Java's AVX-512 Base64 decoder, and Equixly reached the same finding in a separate analysis . The flawed code runs only on x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI support, when untrusted data reaches the basic or URL decoder of java.util.Base64 . ARM servers do not run it.
The code is in Java 17.0.6 and later and in Java 21, 25 and 27, but not in standard Java 8 or 11. A crash is the likely result because the bytes written past the buffer are fixed and not chosen by the attacker. Neither firm reported reproducing the overflow on AVX-512 hardware.
Oracle's 8u371-perf release notes show that its Java 8 Enterprise Performance Pack added a "Base64 Decoding optimization for x86 using AVX-512". Neither firm said whether the Performance Pack is affected.
Both firms named two JVM options as stopgaps to keep the flawed code from running: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics , which turns off the Base64 intrinsics, and -XX:UseAVX=2 , which turns off all AVX-512 code paths and can slow other work. Neither option has been confirmed by a vendor for this flaw, the firms said.
Oracle's November notice covers Oracle products and does not establish the patch status of third-party OpenJDK distributions.
The OpenJDK Vulnerability Group , which coordinates security disclosures affecting OpenJDK source code, had not published an advisory newer than October 24 at the time of the earlier review.
Until official details are available, organizations cannot determine from the reported CVE alone whether their Java deployments are vulnerable or which specific update addresses the issue.
Oracle began a monthly security patch cycle on May 28, introducing targeted security releases between its quarterly Critical Patch Updates.
Its Java security update plan , last updated September 10, identified November 17 as the next scheduled monthly release.
Organizations should inventory deployed Java runtimes, identify internet-facing applications, and prepare to test and install the relevant vendor updates once they become available.
This is a developing story. We will update this article as Oracle publishes its full vulnerability advisory and additional verified details about CVE-2026-114938, affected versions, and available patches emerge.

articles.title_orig: How to Get Ready for November 19
articles.title_zh: How to Get Ready for November 19
articles.content_orig:
November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before.
2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19.
You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too.
XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach.
You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it.
If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do.
We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair.
Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in.
We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify .
XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking .
Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions.
Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.
No seriously, we saw one recently .

articles.title_orig: Apple outages appear to be resolved after internal update takes popular services offline
articles.title_zh: Apple outages appear to be resolved after internal update takes popular services offline
articles.content_orig:
Outages affecting several of Apple’s popular consumer-facing services appeared to be resolved Tuesday night after an internal update caused tech issues for much of the afternoon.
The Apple system status page showed no outages as of 6 p.m. ET. Several hours earlier, around 2 p.m., Apple’s system status page showed that Apple Business, Apple School Manager, AppleCare, iCloud Mail and Web Apps, and SchoolWork were all experiencing outages.
Before that, the page had shown the App Store and Apple Music experiencing outages.
“Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning,” an Apple spokesperson had told NBC News early in the afternoon. “We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible.”
At Apple stores in New York and Chicago, employees told NBC News earlier in the day that their internal software had stopped working and they had been unable to complete purchases or make appointments.
Over the past week, U.S. residents have experienced a cascade of technical issues that have led to nationwide outages of key consumer services, including email, air travel and online banking.
While none of the issues appear to be related, they’ve exposed America’s reliance on older infrastructure and revealed the extent to which companies and governments are being forced to upgrade systems in the AI age. The incidents have also stoked unfounded paranoia that something larger may be afoot.
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.
Kayla Steinberg is a producer at NBC News covering business and the economy.
Madison Lambert is an assignment editor at NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Kuwait reports drone attacks as Iran, US trade attacks on Qeshm and Bahrain
articles.title_zh: Kuwait reports drone attacks as Iran, US trade attacks on Qeshm and Bahrain
articles.content_orig:
Kuwait’s army has said the Gulf country is under attack by drones while the United States and Iran traded blows, marking escalating tensions in the region as a peace deal remains elusive.
The military said in a statement on X on Tuesday that “any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defence systems intercepting hostile attacks”.
The US earlier carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern island of Qeshm, in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after Iran said it launched a drone attack on a US radar system in Bahrain.
“The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, told the official IRNA news agency on Tuesday.
He said the situation was under control and relief agencies were on full alert. IRNA reported five to six explosions on the island on Tuesday evening.
A US official told Al Jazeera the strike hit a missile launch site on Qeshm, in response to Iran’s earlier attack on a US base in Bahrain.
US Central Command said Iranian drones aimed at a US radar system at an air base in Bahrain “were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or personnel”.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it carried out a “precision operation” with drones on the US-operated radar at the Sheikh Isa air base, in response to “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”.
Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, said its air defences intercepted the attack, and blasts were heard over the capital, Manama, according to the AFP news agency.
It was the third Iranian drone attack on Bahrain in five days after a lull of several weeks. Friday’s strike was the first Iranian attack on a Gulf country since early September, AFP reported. Reuters said it came after a Bahraini court sentenced 64 people, mostly Shia clerics, to life in prison for allegedly colluding with Iran.
Kuwait’s armed forces said on Tuesday night that its air defences were responding to “hostile drone attacks” and urged the public to follow safety instructions.
It did not say where the drones came from or whether there were casualties or damage.
Iran’s armed forces said three oil tankers struck naval mines while trying to cross the strait on Tuesday. The US military says it cleared the main routes of mines.
Since the war began on February 28, Iran has tried to restrict traffic through the strait , which normally carries about a fifth of the world’s oil, insisting that ships use only routes it has authorised. The US has responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has escorted tankers.
Another tanker, the Panamanian-flagged Tara Gas, was struck on Monday about seven nautical miles north of Khasab, in Oman, causing a fire in its engine room, according to the security firm Vanguard.
Vanguard and India’s ports minister initially said all 25 crew, 24 of them Indian, were safe. But the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the vessel was hit a second time and the crew were “currently unaccounted for”. India’s ports minister later said the crew had abandoned the vessel after a second attack and that one Indian sailor was missing. Another Panamanian-flagged tanker, the On Phoenix, was hit by an unidentified projectile off Oman’s coast on Monday.
Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and his Omani counterpart, Badr Albusaidi, discussed safeguarding shipping and diplomatic options in Muscat, Oman’s news agencies said.
A third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrived in the Middle East on Monday, and US President Donald Trump is due to hold a three-way summit on Thursday in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where the Iran war is on the agenda.

articles.title_orig: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
articles.title_zh: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
articles.content_orig:
But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.
But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.
But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves , and that this approach is dangerous.
Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”
I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite . Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.
“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”
“Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”
Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”
“I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”
“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”
Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.
Of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.
“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he said.

articles.title_orig: A string of tech outages disrupted flights, banking, and major apps. Here's what officials have said about the causes.
articles.title_zh: A string of tech outages disrupted flights, banking, and major apps. Here's what officials have said about the causes.
articles.content_orig:
If you feel like the digital world is ending , you're not alone.
A string of high-profile technology outages over the past week has disrupted the lives of many Americans trying to travel, transfer money, or make purchases, and caused speculation that something bigger and more nefarious could be going on.
There has been no indication from government officials or the companies affected that cyberattacks or AI were responsible. And despite the uncanny timing, there are no signs the incidents were connected.
"At this point, there is no indication that these incidents are the result of a cyberattack, foreign interference, or some coordinated effort," Sen. Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence committee, said in a statement Tuesday, adding that the evidence suggested the outages were due to "legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity."
Warner said AI was allowing vulnerabilities to be identified faster and creating pressure to fix them immediately, "putting tremendous strain on systems that weren't built to handle that pace of change."
"These disruptions should serve as a wake-up call," he said. "It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences."
Here are the major outages reported and what we know about each one.
Microsoft experienced a major outage last week that impacted its 365 tool suite, affecting products such as Outlook, Teams, and Copilot.
By late Friday morning, the company said services were stabilizing.
Microsoft said the cause of the outage was "technical" and "not related to cyber or AI / agents."
The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, citing issues with its air traffic control systems.
Flights were grounded for over four hours, leading to thousands of delays and cancellations on Friday and Saturday.
Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the outage on aging air traffic control infrastructure.
Mullin said they did not believe the outage was related to cybersecurity or an AI attack.
JPMorgan Chase said Monday said it experienced service issues related to a "software bug in on-premise hardware systems."
Customers had reported issues accessing account information and delayed transactions. Customers of other banks also reported issues, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and US Bank, with the latter saying customers attempting to use Chase's Zelle may have been affected.
"There is no evidence this is cyber-related," Chase said.
United Airlines on Monday said it fixed a "technology issue" after a system outage caused delays to departing flights.
The airline said flights in progress and United Express flights weren't affected. United had 945 delayed flights on Monday, according to the flight tracking site FlightAware.
"There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue," United said.
Charles Schwab experienced issues with its website on Tuesday. Some users were unable to access the site, which temporarily displayed a message that said its server "encountered an internal error or misconfiguration and was unable to complete your request."
The spokesperson for the brokerage firm said a "brief webpage loading issue has been resolved."
Apple said an "internal update" caused outages to some of its services after users online said they were having issues accessing Apple Pay and iCloud.
"Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning," Apple said in a statement. "We're working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible."
Apple said the incident was not a cyberattack.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine cripples Crimean road bridge in blow to Putin before meeting with Xi and Trump
articles.title_zh: Ukraine cripples Crimean road bridge in blow to Putin before meeting with Xi and Trump
articles.content_orig:
With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea
A t 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.
Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.
“We knew what the target was. Everyone was enthusiastic and excited,” one person who took part in the special operation, using the pseudonym “Leon”, told the Guardian. His 7th Deep Strike Centre is part of “Magyar’s Birds”, a brigade named after the call sign of its founder, Robert Brovdi, the head of Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces . Leon said: “Nobody gets excited any more about oil refineries. This was different.”
The soldiers got ready to launch, then watched the biplane-like drone, laden with explosives, disappear across the southern Ukrainian steppe.
Over the next four hours, hundreds of attack drones followed the same linear path, flying first over land and then over the Black Sea. In the early hours of the morning they arrived at their destination: the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia. Putin opened the monumental road and rail crossing in 2018 , driving across it in a Kamaz truck. This was four years after his undercover troops – known as little green men – seized the peninsula.
Russian propagandists had described the bridge as impregnable. It was, they said, an edifice as strong and unyielding as their country’s iron leader. For Ukraine , by contrast, it was a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Also, officials pointed out, it was illegal. Twice Kyiv had tried to blow it up – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.
On this occasion, the Ukrainian military’s careful, multi-stage plan worked perfectly. “It was a well-coordinated operation. Waves of drones started from different locations. The goal was to overwhelm Russia’s well-organised air defence system, rather than the bridge itself,” Leon explained.
As expected, the initial salvo tied up Russia’s local defences. According to insiders, Ukraine then launched a second drone wave. Its function was crucial and different: to act as a relay system for radio signals. Previously, Ukrainian units had used Starshield, the military equivalent of Starlink, for mid-range strikes on occupied territory. Elon Musk’s SpaceX owns the satellite internet network, which is overseen by the Pentagon and the Trump administration.
Ten days ago, however, limits were mysteriously imposed on Ukrainian drones, so they could no longer fly at above 161 km/h (100 mph) . SpaceX insists there is no slowdown – a statement Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, says is untrue . On Monday night, it appears Kyiv bypassed US restrictions by setting up its own extraordinary and innovative real-time video and radio connection.
Once the relay was in place, a third wave of attacks could begin. This time they featured Flamingos, a potent Ukrainian-made cruise missile capable of carrying 1,000kg of explosives – enough to seriously damage the bridge. An unknown number of missiles – some reports say at least four – were launched from southern Ukraine and sent towards Crimea.
A video from one of the Flamingos shows it drawing inexorably towards the target. The onboard camera captures a ghostly night-time scene. The crossing looms into view against a grisaille background. Suddenly a gigantic steel arch appears. The feed cuts out. Other footage shows the moment of impact: an orange fireball, pricking the surrounding blackness.
Photos taken on Tuesday morning in the aftermath of the attack show a scene of watery devastation. A massive arch had tumbled overnight into the Kerch straight , with a large concrete chunk of the road crossing. Nobody will be driving across the bridge anytime soon. The adjacent railway arch span was also damaged. “We were very happy, swapping messages all night,” Leon said.
One source in Ukraine’s armed forces said the timing of the operation – hailed by Zelenskyy as “unprecedented” – was deliberate. It was conducted ahead of a meeting on Thursday between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an Apec summit. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” the person said.
They added: “We understand that what we did shows the world that the king is nude. Putin is weak and vulnerable and we just proved it. The operation was purposefully designed for this specific historic moment. Putin’s plan was to bluff at the summit about how powerful he is. In reality, he can’t even protect the most important and symbolic pillars of his regime.”
In addition to Putin’s political embarrassment before his peers, the disabling of the Kerch bridge has practical consequences. Since annexing Crimea, Russia has militarised the peninsula, effectively turning it into a giant and fortified army base. Since 2022 it has been used as a launch platform for drone and missile attacks on the port of Odesa, and other Ukrainian cities in the region.
Russia’s occupying southern army has relied on the bridge for regular deliveries of ammunition, equipment and fuel. With the crossing partially closed – rail travel reportedly reopened on Tuesday – Russia will have to use an under fire land corridor instead, connecting its Rostov oblast with the Moscow-controlled parts of Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia and Kherson provinces.
“We have disrupted their logistics to Crimea. There will be a lot of problems for Russia’s army in the south,” Leon predicted. Debris from the bridge strike is obstructing the narrow shipping corridor through the Kerch strait, linking the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. The Azov sea now resembles a lake. Passenger ferries are unable to move, with the occupied ports of Mariupol and Berdyansk cut off.
The soldiers returned from their mission jubilant and elated. Back at their headquarters, they gathered as usual for a minute’s silence, in memory of those killed in Russia’s bloody war. “We had our daily ritual as usual. Then there were congratulations on a very successful and important operation,” Leon said. Then he added: “We are paying them back.”

articles.title_orig: Nvidia earnings call offers a crucial clue about who could succeed Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: Nvidia earnings call offers a crucial clue about who could succeed Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
A pivotal Nvidia earnings call offered a crucial clue as to who could succeed Jensen Huang .
After prepared remarks from interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones during Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday, a notable participant was introduced: Ian Buck , Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, who joined Kress for the Q&A session.
Buck, an Nvidia veteran who helped invent its CUDA software for AI chips, had been floated by industry observers as a potential successor to Huang . He didn't end up saying anything on the call.
His appearance came as Jones reiterated that Nvidia's board does not intend to reinstate Huang and that the board hired the search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find his successor from both internal and external candidates.
"We want to install the CEO, the permanent CEO, as quickly as possible, but we won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person," Jones said.
Buck has worked at Nvidia for more than two decades. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan previously told Business Insider that Buck was one of Huang's three "right-hand men" — along with Kress and senior VP of GPU engineering Jonah Alben.
That said, Stephen Witt, who wrote a biography on Huang, said Buck is less focused on business strategy.
"He's more like the world's best mechanic," Witt said.
Earlier in the day, Huang broke his silence and expressed his desire to return to the company — so long as the board approved.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
On the call, Jones said the company would not take questions on the circumstances of Huang's resignation or the ongoing investigation. That said, Kress addressed it briefly when talking about the impacts on employee retention.
She said there are "diverse opinions," though employees remain committed to their work.
Huang's ouster has sent shockwaves through the AI sector, the broader markets, and the global economy. The stock has plunged as investors try to get to grips with a future without the vision, connections, and technical knowledge of Huang, who led the company for more than 30 years.
Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes called Buck Nvidia's strongest potential internal successor given his work on CUDA, stewardship of the chip giant's massive data center business, and relationships with top cloud customers.
Business Insider asked Dan Ives, a tech analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co., whether putting Buck on the earnings call signaled that this Nvidia executive is a candidate for the new CEO role.
"His hat is in the ring," Ives said.

articles.title_orig: Student accused of taking photos of planes for Chinese Communist Party to be detained pending trial
articles.title_zh: Student accused of taking photos of planes for Chinese Communist Party to be detained pending trial
articles.content_orig:
A college student accused of working with a Chinese Communist Party representative to take photos of American airplanes and logistic hubs in Chicago — and lying about it to U.S. investigators — will be detained pending trial, a federal judge ruled Tuesday.
Detroit-based federal Magistrate Judge Kimberly Altman denied a request from lawyers for Weiheng Zeng, a Chinese citizen who is currently an undergraduate at the University of Waterloo in Ontario, to remain free and return to Canada as his case proceeds.
According to the Justice Department, Zeng's legal team said in a court hearing Tuesday that his family would "pay any bond amount this court could impose" to keep their client out of detention, and suggested the family could even buy an apartment in the United States for Zeng to be bonded to.
Zeng was indicted earlier this month on one count of making false statements to a government agency. Prosecutors allege he sneaked into a FedEx property at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport and took photos of the facility, then later lied about the purpose of his trip to the United States to customs officials, calling it "hobby photography."
Zeng pleaded not guilty earlier this month . He hasn't explicitly been charged with taking photos of planes, but instead was charged with lying to investigators.
A criminal complaint filed in the Eastern District of Michigan alleges that in April, Zeng took photographs of the FedEx facility, climbed on a parked forklift and attempted to open locked trailers. The Justice Department says surveillance footage shows Zeng attempting to open a shipping container and using the forklift to take photos at a higher vantage point.
After leaving the country, Zeng attempted to reenter the U.S. on Aug. 23 through Detroit's Ambassador Bridge, which links Canada and Michigan, and was flagged for additional screening based on the April incident. He was then interviewed three subsequent times by Customs and Border Protection agents.
In his third interview, Zeng stated that a Chinese contact assigned him specific planes and tail numbers to photograph and that he would be paid between $20 and $30 per photo, according to the criminal complaint. Zeng said that he talked to the contact using SIM cards that were sent to him by mail, and after talking, he would destroy the SIM cards, delete the conversations and delete the photos that he had taken.
He allegedly told customs officers that the contact approached him on an "aviation spotter website" and said he believed the person was connected to the Chinese Communist Party, and was told that the photos were going to be used for "research."
Zeng was then interviewed by the FBI, the complaint says. He allegedly told law enforcement the contact was interested in getting photographs of rare airplanes, and believed the contact worked for the Chinese government because "when he started making more requests, the language he used was very organized and managed, not language typically used between friends." The photos, Zeng said, were also of "American United" aircraft at O'Hare.
Federal investigators said it was only after further questioning from the FBI that Zeng admitted that he had messaged with the contact for three months and said he wanted to help the contact because "he thought it was 'cool' and wanted 'to have the opportunity to work with someone like [agents] at the FBI.'"
He told the FBI that the contact wanted him to find out more about transportation and logistics in the United States, and wanted him to travel to Orlando, Las Vegas and Los Angeles to "obtain photographs of specific locations surrounding airports."
Zeng said he denied those tasks.
His lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the detention order.

articles.title_orig: Sean Duffy’s $50 billion demand for air travel fixes is met with yelling and skepticism in Congress
articles.title_zh: Sean Duffy’s $50 billion demand for air travel fixes is met with yelling and skepticism in Congress
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — The Trump administration’s request for $50.1 billion in new Federal Aviation Administration funding after a nationwide ground stop strangled air travel is running into skepticism from both parties on Capitol Hill.
The funding request was suddenly increased from $30 billion after the hourslong ground stop Friday caused delays and cancellations for passengers across thousands of flights.
The formal funding ask was conveyed in a Tuesday letter signed by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who refused to apologize or accept responsibility for the failure, blaming it on predecessors and Congress. The letter, cosigned by FAA chief Bryan Bedford and White House budget director Russell Vought, stated the money was needed “to deliver a truly world-class air traffic control network.”
After publicly reproaching Congress for the failure last week, Duffy met privately with Senate Republicans on Tuesday to make his case on Capitol Hill.
The closed-door briefing was contentious. The transportation secretary was “yelled at” by multiple Republican senators during his briefing, according to a person in the room who was not authorized to speak publicly about the private discussion.
When it was over, Senate Republican leaders and Duffy notably held their news conferences separately.
Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., stopped short of endorsing the full funding figure, saying only that the GOP is unified around the belief that “safe skies is an incredibly important priority.”
“We will see what the traffic will bear, what’s achievable,” he said, calling it a “discussion to be had” on the dollar amount.
Duffy met with only Republicans on Tuesday, not Democrats — even though the regular government funding process requires bipartisan support.
And Democrats were left wanting a better explanation, particularly as Duffy has pointed fingers at them. And members in both parties noted that President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” included $12.5 billion for air traffic control that still has not been fully used up.
“Look, we have not been given the answers. They have not come clean,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., told reporters on Tuesday. “At his first press conference, all Duffy did was attack Democrats, and he asked for $50 billion when they haven’t even spent the $12 billion we’ve given to them. I have little faith in them.”
Facing Republican questions on the matter, Duffy insisted that the $12.5 billion was insufficient for the specific upgrades he deemed necessary in this situation.
Other Democrats are vexed by the FAA funding request.
“I generally support the idea of investing in air traffic control, but $50 billion sounds like an awfully round number,” said Sen. Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, who’s poised to become majority whip and also sits on the Senate Appropriations Committee.
The issue is wrapped up in a larger debate about funding the government ahead of a Dec. 11 deadline to avoid another shutdown . Congress could either reach a deal by then on new funding, punt it to next year with a stopgap bill, or fail to act and allow a shutdown.
Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, said air traffic control is “absolutely not a partisan issue” and that Congress will work to make sure that any funding is “paid for in a responsible way.”
Republicans are also considering a party-line “reconciliation” bill to approve military funding without the need for Democratic votes; Democrats are likely to resist additional military funds unless the Iran war comes to an end. Other provisions could be added to such a bill — if it materializes before Republicans lose control of Congress. Thune indicated Tuesday that it is still an open question, as Republicans would need to pass a budget resolution by Thanksgiving to pull it off. It would be a long, arduous process requiring near-total GOP unity in both chambers, and it would need to begin soon in order to finish this year.
Duffy said he’s agnostic on how the funds get passed when asked by NBC News why he only met with Republicans on Tuesday.
“I have met with Democrats. I’ve spent hours on the phone with Democrats. Get along with them well. They understand this issue,” Duffy said Tuesday, speaking to reporters separately after meeting with GOP senators. “I’m not going to tell them how to do their work, but I’m telling everybody what we need. I’m making a nice ask, and I’m going to let them work their process.”
One of the Democrats whom Duffy spoke to was House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely next House speaker.
“I appreciated the conversation,” Jeffries told reporters. “There are still more questions than answers in terms of what happened, why it happened, how do we prevent it from happening again.”
Jeffries added that he wants a briefing on the FAA ground stop and other recent outages, saying: “These developments are troubling, and it’s unclear if it’s all infrastructure-related or whether there’s some malignant activity.”
When asked about Duffy’s $50.1 billion request, outgoing House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said Republicans would work with the administration to fund “as much of that as we can.” He pointed to the $12.5 billion already approved for FAA modernization and did not specify a timeline or whether Congress would pursue a supplemental funding package.
I am a field producer for NBC News based in Washington, D.C., covering all things politics.
Sahil Kapur is a senior national political reporter for NBC News.
Julie Tsirkin is a correspondent covering Capitol Hill and the White House.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.title_zh: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.
“At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months.
Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history.
The platform, which serves more than 18 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the company’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.”
So far, Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call.
“Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” said Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face.
Last week, Nvidia founder Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He’s also accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is now set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, The WSJ reported .
Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On today’s call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the “most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter,” and it’s “where developers start to build their own intelligence.”
“That foundation is empowering the ecosystem,” she said.
Correction: Due to a typo, an earlier version of this article incorrectly stated the number of developers served by Hugging Face; it is 18 million, not 118 million.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia: China fears Jensen Huang scandal could shut it out of US AI tech before Xi-Trump summit
articles.title_zh: Nvidia: China fears Jensen Huang scandal could shut it out of US AI tech before Xi-Trump summit
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang is out but his shadow looms over the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week.
For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures.
Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship.
US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency.
The claim remains unproven, but it has already reignited debate in Washington over exports of advanced chips to China and whether the Trump administration has been too willing to ease restrictions.
For years now, advanced computer chips have been a key battleground in the US-China rivalry because they are essential for AI, supercomputing and military technology.
Chinese officials are worried this scandal could strengthen voices in Washington who argue in favour of further limiting Chinese access to cutting-edge American tech.
Just this week, the Trump administration introduced new export restrictions on Chinese firms that access advanced US chips in third countries such as Malaysia, Thailand or Brazil. They typically do this by renting computing power in data centres abroad to train their AI models. But some of the firms, like the one Alice Huang worked for, are also accused of smuggling chips to China, although they have denied this.
Until now, this controversy appeared to be a sideshow in US-China relations. But with Beijing calling the new rules "economic coercion" on the eve of Trump arriving in Shenzhen, there is a growing risk it could become something much bigger.
Watch: Jensen Huang speaks to the BBC's Faisal Islam in 2025
Democrats, who will control Congress come January, have made their position clear. Last Wednesday top Democrat Ted Lieu told Politico the Trump administration had been "1,000%" too deferential to Nvidia, putting national security at risk, while fellow Democrat Zoe Lofgren suggested Congress would now be more likely to restrict sales of AI chips to China.
The BBC has approached the White House for comment.
Beijing's foreign ministry had described the spy claims as a "smear against China".
"The US should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives to find pretexts for imposing technological blockades," spokesperson Mao Ning said last week.
The ministry also seemed keen to keep the meeting on track, saying the two countries had kept "close communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state".
For the last year, Trump and Xi have been seeking to stabilise relations after a damaging tariff war that almost brought trade between the two countries to a standstill.
The Trump administration's decision to permit sales of advanced Nvidia H200 chips to China in late 2025 was seen as evidence that both sides were searching for areas of co-operation, even while competition intensified.
It was a rare move given Washington had spent years trying to limit China's access to the most advanced chips.
Many in the US have long viewed these chips as a national security issue, arguing they could strengthen China's military and surveillance capabilities. Jensen Huang, who rejects that claim , advocated lifting bans on the export of high-performing chips to China. Beijing argues the restrictions are an attempt to contain its rise.
Now that opening may be under threat.
History has taught Beijing and Washington that spy scandals rarely remain confined to the intelligence world.
Analysts in China already see echoes of an incident in 2023 when a suspected surveillance balloon drifted through the skies over the US before an American fighter jet shot it down. Beijing insisted it was a civilian meteorological airship that had strayed off course.
The suspected Chinese spy balloon was shot down days after it was spotted over the US
But a planned trip by then US Secretary of State Antony Blinken was cancelled and communication between the two governments deteriorated sharply.
The incident showed how quickly a security dispute could overwhelm diplomatic efforts and push relations into a deep freeze.
"The mere passage of a balloon sent American public opinion and politicians into a state of high alert, as if a "Chinese threat" were looming directly overhead," said the state media outlet, the Global Times this week as it made a direct comparison with the Nvidia scandal.
"No-one on the US side has ever apologised or taken responsibility for the genuine damage this caused to US-China relations," it added.
The state-run outlet also questioned why the Nvidia story had emerged so soon after "the hard-won detente" between Beijing and Washington, following a meeting between the two countries' leaders in September.
"Is someone behind the scenes pushing an agenda and stirring up confrontation?" it asked.
Both Trump and Xi have significant incentives to keep talking.
China's economy remains under pressure and is increasingly reliant on exports. Xi needs trade to keep flowing and this meeting is a key stepping stone to replacing the current trade truce that is due to expire in January.
Meanwhile Trump has repeatedly touted his close relationship with Xi and argued that maintaining dialogue is essential to managing competition between the two powers.
The US president is in his last two years and faces an uphill struggle to pass domestic legislation after the midterms. To counter this, he could be looking for some foreign policy wins.
He may also hope for Xi's help to end the war in the Middle East.
Neither side will want to be discussing intelligence concerns and technology controls instead of trade, investment and economic co-operation.
The summit is also being carefully choreographed by Beijing to show off its technological prowess in Shenzhen - a deeply symbolic choice of city.
It's home to some of the country's biggest tech companies and has become a showcase for Beijing's ambitions in AI and advanced manufacturing.
Also, given Washington's tighter restrictions on advanced chips, Beijing has options for retaliation.
One of its most powerful tools is its dominance of key rare earth minerals. China processes much of the world's supply for materials that are used in everything from electric vehicles and smartphones to military equipment.
Analysts have long warned that technological restrictions can trigger a cycle of retaliation in which each side reaches for its strongest economic leverage.
That would shift the current trend of US-China relations from engagement back towards mutual suspicion.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market News, Nov. 17, 2026: Dow ends down 850 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq also plunge as tech names come under further pressure ahead of Nvidia’s earnings
articles.title_zh: Stock Market News, Nov. 17, 2026: Dow ends down 850 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq also plunge as tech names come under further pressure ahead of Nvidia’s earnings
articles.content_orig:
U.S. equities tumbled on Tuesday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite hitting its lowest level in roughly seven months, as traders sold off semiconductor names ahead of Nvidia's much-anticipated earnings report.
Reports of a National Security Agency network outage added to recent jitters about the stability of the country's technology infrastructure and helped weigh on the market, traders said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to end at 50,759.42. It dropped more than 1,000 points at its session low. The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, for its lowest closing level since late July. The broad market index sank as low as 1.7% earlier in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.74%. At one point during Tuesday's session, it sank by as much as roughly 2.1% to touch its lowest level since April.
Major averages fell to their lows of the day following the report from CNN that said a classified network used by the spy agency had gone down, citing six people familiar with the matter. CNN's sources said there was no evidence that it was a cyberattack.
The NSA later in the day put out a statement saying the agency "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance." The agency added that "mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational."
Traders said the report helped take equities lower, though the losses were contained. This outage is latest in a string of incidents that have left people on edge including the FAA ground stop over the weekend, Microsoft's Outlook outage last week and some recent issues with banking apps.
Nvidia shares ended the session 0.5% lower amid investors' handwringing ahead of the company's earnings report due after the closing bell. However, the stock got a short-lived boost earlier in the session after Jensen Huang said he would be open to returning as CEO if the company's board thought that was in the best interest of shareholders.
"Nvidia should report strong results and guidance, but [it] is unlikely to be able to give investors solid answers to the questions heavily weighing on the stock [regarding] leadership and investigations around export controls," Ross Mayfield, investment strategist at Baird, told CNBC. "Strong demand might stabilize things, but the next leg higher will need some clarification around the 2028 and beyond outlook."
Other tech players ended the day in negative territory but well off their session lows, with Micron Technology sliding 0.9%. Advanced Micro Devices slipped 0.2%, while Intel was down 0.5%.
Microsoft shares were down 2%.
Neocloud stock Iren shed more than 3%. Nebius lost 1%. Investor Steve Eisman told CNBC earlier in the day that these stocks were among the names with the most to lose if the Huang scandal causes Nvidia to pull back its financing of the AI ecosystem.
U.S. equities closed lower on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 848.75 points, or 1.64%, lower at 50,759.42. It fell more than 1,000 points at its session low.
The S&P 500 shed 1.03% to end the session at 7,340.53, for its lowest closing level since late July. The broad market index sank as low as 1.73% earlier in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite was down 0.74% to 24,328.38 at the closing bell. At one point, it sank by as much as roughly 2.1% to hit its lowest level since April.
The VIX volatility index , a gauge of how much the S&P 500 might move in the next 30 days based on options trading, rose as much as 21% to an intraday high of 27.73, the highest since Nov. 6.
The VIX is now on track to rise for a fourth consecutive day for the first time since August 28.
Recent market volatility doesn't change UBS' conviction in the opportunity in artificial intelligence or its constructive view on diversified equities.
Investors weighing AI demand and the elevated capital expenditures from tech companies have sent stocks lower.
"Still, for the sell-off to indicate a lasting deterioration in the AI investment cycle, we would need to see weakening compute demand, slowing AI- related revenue growth, poor capacity utilization, or tighter financial conditions constraining spending by the largest technology platforms, Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, chief investment officer for Americas, said in a note Tuesday.
Breadth of selling will also matter, and there is no evidence of that yet. Underlying demand for computing capacity also remains robust, he noted.
"We therefore continue to see potential for gains in broad equity markets over the next six to 12 months, supported by resilient economic growth and corporate earnings," Hoffmann-Burchardi wrote. "Near-term volatility reinforces the importance of selectivity and disciplined portfolio construction rather than a broadly defensive stance."
A CNN report Tuesday that a classified network used by the National Security Agency is down was just the latest to hit a stock market that's been battered lately by negative headlines. These include the FAA ground stop over the weekend, as well as Microsoft's Outlook outage last week.
"Any one of the stories that have have broken over the course of the last week or so would be enough to cause the market jitters. But when you compound that by having multiple stories — whether it's today's NSA report or the FAA ground halt or Microsoft Outlook being down for two days or Chase Bank ATMs not working — aggregate all of those, and it's easy for the human mind to get to a place where there must be something larger at play here," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. "What's causing the market to have the kind of drawdowns that it's having today, it's just that aggregate of the compounding of bizarre stories that just have become too much of a headwind, at least in the near term," he added.
Investors may not be moved by Nvidia's upcoming earnings results, according to Megan Horneman, chief investment officer at Verdence Capital Advisors.
"I don't think there's going to be anything surprising from the earnings report," she told CNBC. "I don't know that we're even going to get much forward-looking information that people may be trying to get information on."
Horneman expects uncertainty to persist for the technology sector as investors assess what the trade could look like after "parts of Nvidia start to unwind."
"We're just stuck in this, I think, panic type of stage right now, and I don't know how far it will go," she said.
Another strong round of economic data, particularly on the consumer side, has led Goldman Sachs to take up its growth forecast.
The firm now sees  fourth quarter gross domestic product accelerating by a 2.4% annualized pace, up 0.6 percentage point from its prior outlook. Moreover, Goldman raised its backward-looking expectation for the third quarter, now looking for 3.8% growth from the period, which would be 0.4 percentage point higher than the advance estimate from the Commerce Department.
At the core of the more optimistic outlook is a retail sales report Tuesday that showed receipts up 0.2% in October — 0.6% when excluding autos and when focusing on the components that feed directly to GDP.
"The strength of today's report continues to reflect the resilience of the US consumer this year, as boosts from tax refunds and positive wealth effects from equity market gains have more than offset the drag from higher energy prices," Goldman chief economist Jan Hatzius said in a note.
Selling was broad across Wall Street midday Tuesday as declining stocks outnumbered advancers by nearly 3 to 1 on both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq.
Declining volume accounted for roughly 69% of total NYSE volume and 71% on the Nasdaq, according to FactSet data.
On the NYSE, 1,924 stocks declined while only 700 rose. For Nasdaq, decliners totaled 3,036, compared with 1,141 advancers.
New lows also outpaced new highs. The NYSE recorded 362 new lows against just 20 new highs, while the Nasdaq logged 679 new lows versus 38 new highs.
— Deena Zaidi and Scott Schnipper

articles.title_orig: Fed official Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House firing hearing, citing bias
articles.title_zh: Fed official Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House firing hearing, citing bias
articles.content_orig:
United States Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has declined, through her lawyers, to appear next month before a Trump administration committee that is considering whether she should be fired, calling the process unfair and committed to a predetermined outcome.
The refusal extends the wrangling between the White House and Cook’s lawyers regarding her appearance before the committee, which the administration of US President Donald Trump initially demanded for November 6.
Administration officials have called on Cook to appear before the committee to address allegations that she committed mortgage fraud in 2021, before she joined the Fed’s board of governors, a charge she denies. Cook has not been charged with any crime.
Trump has sought to fire Cook since August 2025, and she has argued that the president’s efforts to do so represent a threat to the Fed’s independence and reflect Trump’s desire to force the central bank to reduce borrowing costs.
“Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution’s unique status and independence,” Abbe David Lowell, Cook’s lawyer, wrote in a letter released on Tuesday to White House counsel William Scharf. The three-person panel set up by the White House to consider the allegations “appears to be a facade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook”, the letter said.
In June, the US Supreme Court blocked Trump from removing Cook while litigation over the attempted firing continues, finding that “the fact of independence but also the appearance of independence is key to the Federal Reserve’s design”.
Trump officials have threatened to move ahead with the hearing even without Cook, and in a November 3 letter said that the three-member committee “reserves the right to draw adverse inferences against you” for not participating.
The unusual “committee of inquiry” set up by the White House consists of Kevin Hassett, Trump’s top economic adviser; Andrea Lucas, whom Trump appointed to lead the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission; and Keith Sonderling, Trump’s pick for Department of Labor secretary.
The Supreme Court said in a footnote to its June ruling that Trump could try again to fire Cook if the administration provided her adequate notice and an opportunity to respond. The committee of inquiry is an effort to meet those conditions.
Under the law governing the Fed, the president can only fire a Fed governor “for cause”, but the Supreme Court didn’t address whether Cook’s actions met that standard. The committee will ultimately recommend whether there is cause to fire Cook, the White House has said.

articles.title_orig: Sheinbaum and Xi meet in Shenzhen to mark a ‘new era,’ advance Mexico-China relations
articles.title_zh: Sheinbaum and Xi meet in Shenzhen to mark a ‘new era,’ advance Mexico-China relations
articles.content_orig:
In a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Tuesday, President Claudia Sheinbaum declared that her visit to China marks “a new era” in Mexico’s relationship with the East Asian country.
She also told the Chinese president and general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party she was “convinced” that the bilateral meeting would “strengthen collaboration” between the Mexican and Chinese governments and the Mexican and Chinese people. In subsequent remarks to reporters , Sheinbaum described her meeting with Xi as “very good” and “very, very frank.”
For his part, Xi told Sheinbaum that China and Mexico are “good friends” and that advancing relations is “important for both countries,” according to a readout published by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs .
The two leaders and members of their respective cabinets met in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting, which starts in the southern Chinese city on Wednesday. Sheinbaum previously met with Xi at the G20 leaders’ summit in Brazil in November 2024 .
In public remarks to Xi , Sheinbaum thanked the Chinese president for his invitation to the APEC CEO Summit, at which she spoke on Tuesday .
She noted that Mexico will host the APEC Leaders’ Meeting in 2028 and told Xi it would be a “pleasure” to welcome him to that event.
Sheinbaum said that the Mexico-China relationship is “the result of deep bonds of friendship and shared principles, such as cooperation, development and shared prosperity.”
“Mexico and China share a vision of development and prosperity, and our nations have strengthened their relationship in order to cooperate on a variety of issues,” she said.
“On this occasion, we are interested in strengthening cooperation in areas related to science and technology, agriculture, clean energy, water resources, health and, of course, culture and tourism,” Sheinbaum said.
According to a statement issued by Mexico’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE), Sheinbaum and Xi “highlighted opportunities to deepen bilateral cooperation on health, river cleanup and restoration, sustainable water management, biodiversity conservation, waste management guided by circular economy principles , the fight against climate change and the development of resilient cities, as Shenzhen’s model shows.”
In China, Mexico’s environment minister takes notes on its waste-to-energy circular economy
“They also agreed to strengthen scientific cooperation by training talent, conducting joint research in strategic areas such as mathematics, agriculture, biotechnology and clean energy, and developing bilateral initiatives, including the Young Scientists Exchange Program,” the SRE said.
The ministry also said that Sheinbaum and Xi “expressed their desire to keep strengthening” the Mexico-China relationship through the two countries’ Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which was launched by Xi and former Mexican President Enrique Peña Nieto in 2013 .
Mexico and China don’t have a free trade agreement, and the former country angered the latter when it imposed new and higher tariffs on Chinese goods at the start of 2026 .
Mexico’s tariffs on China — seen in part as an effort to appease U.S. President Donald Trump, who has accused Mexico of being a transshipment hub for Chinese goods — were not mentioned by the SRE or the Chinese Foreign Ministry in their statements.
The SRE did say that the Mexican and Chinese presidents “discussed opportunities to deepen trade,” adding that Sheinbaum “said Mexico is interested in moving toward a more balanced and diversified economic relationship.”
China’s exports to Mexico — which include electronic equipment and electric vehicles — are worth far more than its imports from Mexico, leaving it with a large trade surplus . Some imports from China pose a threat to Mexican manufacturing sectors, giving the Mexican government added incentive to impose higher tariffs on them.
Sheinbaum told reporters in Shenzhen that she and Xi had spoken about increasing Mexico’s exports of various products to China, “from avocados to tequila.”
Asked whether she and the Chinese president spoke about Mexico’s relationship with the United States, the president responded:
“The issue was raised, but we always talk about our trade agreement with the United States, and [say] that we will always do what is best for Mexico.”
The statement issued by the Chinese Foreign Ministry said that “given the complex and volatile global landscape, advancing China-Mexico relations at a higher level, across wider areas, and in greater depth is important for both countries as they implement their respective national development strategies and promote unity for strength among the Global South.”
The ministry said that in his meeting with Sheinbaum, “President Xi stressed that China and Mexico should first continue to treat each other with sincerity, deepen political mutual trust, keep growing bilateral relations in the right direction, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all areas and at all levels, and work together to ensure the success of events celebrating the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations next year.”
The Chinese Foreign Ministry also said that “Mexico firmly adheres to the one-China principle and attaches great importance to its relations with China.”
“In the course of implementing Plan México , Mexico is ready to strengthen cooperation with China in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, manufacturing, artificial intelligence, agriculture and water conservancy and promote exchanges in health, education, culture and tourism, so as to elevate bilateral relations to a new height,” the ministry added.
While Mexico is clearly seeking to strengthen — and broaden — its relationship with China, Sheinbaum is mindful of the need to safeguard Mexico’s relationship with the United States, its largest trade partner. For example, the president — who will meet with Trump in Shenzhen on Wednesday — has made it clear that Mexico is not seeking a free trade agreement with China , the world’s second largest economy.
One apparent motive for China to seek closer ties with Mexico is the country’s proximity to Beijing’s foremost strategic rival — the United States.
In remarks to reporters after her meeting with Xi, Sheinbaum noted that a Chinese company is supplying trains to Mexico ( for the under-construction Mexico City-Pachuca railroad ) and reiterated that Mexico is “very interested” in learning more about China’s “ smart hospitals .”

— Quadratín México (@QuadratinMexico) November 17, 2026
She subsequently revealed that she asked Xi for a panda for the Chapultepec Zoo, located in Chapultepec Park in Mexico City.
One panda, a female called Xin Xin , already lives at the zoo. She was born at the Chapultepec Zoo in 1990.
Given that Mexico and China are on friendly terms and seeking even closer ties, it would appear likely that China will grant Sheinbaum’s request for a panda. According to Reuters , since its founding in 1949, “the People’s Republic of China has used panda diplomacy to boost its international image, either by gifting or lending pandas to foreign zoos as goodwill animal ambassadors.”

The official said the strikes are in response to IRGC attacks.
Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.
Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities.
See the most recent developments below.
Kuwaiti air defenses are countering hostile drone attacks, the Kuwait Army said.
The General Staff of the Army said any explosions heard were the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks.
The U.S. conducted airstrikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Tuesday, targeting launchers in response to IRGC targeting of U.S. personnel and assets, according to a U.S. military official.
"U.S. Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region," the official said.
A tanker transiting in the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly struck for a second time, which caused a fire onboard, a maritime security agency reported to the UKMTO.
This comes after a third party reported an attack on the same vessel on Monday, which resulted in the vessel being disabled and resulted in an engine room fire, according to the UKMTO.
The crew are currently unaccounted for and a damage assessment is currently unknown, according to the UKMTO.
"Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, whilst authorities investigate," the UKMTO said in an update Tuesday.
U.S. Central Command said on Tuesday that air defenses defeated an Iranian drone attack that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said targeted an American radar facility in Bahrain.
"Multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel. CENTCOM and partner forces remain highly vigilant," the command said in a post to X.
